$comment: Gemfall beat 1, The Spark. Story: docs/campaigns/gemfall.md §1. Wiring: docs/campaigns/gemfall-authoring.md. Must set on every path to every ending: exactly one motive_* (choice_why_north, which every path passes through) and exactly one of ember_sold / ember_kept (choice_ember, which every path passes through). The six motive votes each land on a short result scene (scene_motive_*) before the docks, so the vote is seen to matter at the table. No combat: the Exchange is people, prices and promises.
title: The City That Smelled Opportunity

objectives.label: Listened to the scholar everyone laughed at
Heard the rumors of all three roads north
Signed on as real caravan crew

facet_ember.name: The Ember Facet
facet_ember.text: A red stone, warm as toast, that fell from the sky into an Exchange gutter by your boot.

scene_prologue_realm.narration: This is the Realm of Red Sky. Far in the north stands Mount Red Sky, the biggest mountain anybody knows. Old maps call it the Source of the Gemfalls, and add, in much smaller writing, that it is only sleeping.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_city.narration: Far in the south, where every road and river runs down to the sea, is the Exchange: a busy city of towers, bridges and docks, where travelers from all over the realm come to trade, swap news, and find adventure. Nobody is from here. That is rather the point of it.

choices.label: Go on

scene_prologue_party.narration: And this is you: a little band of adventurers who met on the docks this week. Nobody has called you heroes yet. You each came here for a reason of your own, and you have not quite told each other what it is. Tonight is a quiet night, and the harbor lamps are just coming on.

choices.label: Let's begin!

scene_red_sky.narration: It is a quiet night at the Exchange, and then it isn't. Far to the north, the sky over Mount Red Sky turns red as a cherry, and a glittering rain of gem-light falls over the foothills. For one blink, some of it seems to fall up. A seagull drops its fish in surprise, and the fish looks surprised too.

choices.label: Fly up the lighthouse for a better look
Watch from the harbor wall
Run down to the docks and see what people do

scene_lighthouse.narration: From the top of the lighthouse the gem-light falls slow as snow. Then, just for a moment, one thread of it rises back toward the mountain, like a kite string being reeled in. The lighthouse keeper, a very old merfolk in a bathtub, says she did not see that. Neither did you. Officially.

choices.label: Glide back down and see what the city does

scene_harbour_wall.narration: From the harbor wall you watch the whole city find out at once. Every ship in the harbor swings on its anchor until its nose points north, as if the boats are thinking about it too. Bells ring on three towers, then stop, because nobody knows which ring this is. On the lighthouse, the great lamp goes dark for a moment, the way you might close your eyes rather than see something. Then it comes back on and pretends it did not.

choices.label: Watch the red fade, and see what the morning brings

scene_night_docks.narration: The docks are awake before the red has even faded. A boy on a ladder is already rubbing out the price of rope and writing a bigger one. A barrel on wheels rumbles past in the dark with a merfolk inside it, shouting "Rush prices, darlings, rush prices!" to nobody in particular yet. A yeti fishmonger looks north, looks at his herring, and quietly doubles the price of herring.

choices.label: Find a crate to sit on and watch it all begin

scene_stampede.narration: Three days later the Exchange is so full you can't see the cobbles. Merchants, scholars, pilgrims and pickpockets pour in from every road and every ship, all saying the same word: gems. The chalkboard prices change while you read them. A pie now costs as much as a tent, and a tent costs as much as a pony, and the pony has gone north with everybody else.

choices.label: Read the brass plaques on the harbor
Find somewhere to sit and talk

scene_plaques.narration: Seventeen brass plaques stand around the harbor. Each one says who founded the Exchange, and each one names somebody different: a faun, a frogfolk, a family of selkies, and one that just says "my nan". Nobody is from here, so everybody is from here. A centaur tour guide says that is the best thing about the city, and charges you a copper for telling you.

choices.label: Find somewhere to sit and talk

choice_why_north.narration: At a noodle stall you find the one empty chair. Every table in the Exchange keeps one, for whoever arrives next, and today that is you. Everyone in the whole city is going north. So why is our party going north? Everybody vote.

choices.label: For the treasure. Gems, gems, gems!
To find out what really happened
So everyone will know our names
Because somebody has to keep folk safe
For a fresh start somewhere new
To prove we can do it

scene_motive_wealth.narration: "Gems," says Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall. He stirs the pot one whole slow turn before he says anything else. Then he chalks a new line on his board, RUSH PRICES, and your noodles cost twice what they did a minute ago. The crowd cheers you. Three pickpockets move one table closer. A merchant by the door writes your names down and underlines them.

choices.label: Go and find out what gems are fetching at the docks

scene_motive_curiosity.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, stops stirring, which he never does. "The gull," he says. "Dropped its fish before the light got here. Heard something first." He has clearly been thinking about this for three days. He tips your bowl so the soup slops into the shape of the mountain, and taps the top of it with one enormous finger.

choices.label: Go and ask the docks what they heard

scene_motive_prestige.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, turns round, very slowly, and writes your names on the specials board under TODAY'S HEROES. He spells one of them wrong. The whole stall applauds. A very small faun asks you to sign her dumpling, and you do, and she eats it straight away so nobody can steal it.

choices.label: Go where the news is made: the docks

scene_motive_duty.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, says nothing at all. He just fills a fourth bowl and sets it on your table. "For whoever needs it," he rumbles. The whoever turns out to be a faun at the next table whose field caravan left without her, and by the time she has finished the bowl she has told you every road north and which one her cousins are on.

choices.label: Walk her down to the docks and find her a wagon

scene_motive_fresh_start.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, reaches under your table with one slow hand and scratches three marks on the underside of the empty chair. "It's yours now," he says. "Everyone at the Exchange started over. Some of us twice." He gives you the heel of the bread for nothing, which at rush prices is practically a house.

choices.label: Take your first steps as new people: down to the docks

scene_motive_proving.narration: Mortar, the stone troll who runs the noodle stall, points at a bowl on the top shelf that is the size of a bath. "Nobody finishes the Big Bowl," he says. You finish the Big Bowl. It takes all afternoon, and somebody has to be rolled off their chair at the end, but you finish it. "Hm," says Mortar, which from a stone troll is a round of applause.

choices.label: Waddle down to the docks, victorious

scene_docks.narration: The docks are where the Exchange trades its news. Here nobody asks where a thing came from, only where it is going. A boggart in a coat made of other coats is selling "slightly used rumors, hardly heard". A yeti fishmonger shouts the price of herring and, in between herrings, the price of roads.

choices.label: Swap rumors with the dock folk
Buy a rumor from the boggart
Read the crowd and hear what nobody says out loud

check_rumours.prompt: Trade a good rumor for three better ones

onSuccess.narration: You trade the story about the seagull and the surprised fish, and the dock folk like it so much they pay you back three times over.

onFailure.narration: Nobody wants your rumor. In the end you trade your lunch for theirs, which is a fair price, because their rumors are better than your lunch.

scene_boggart.narration: The boggart's rumors come in little jars with the lids screwed on tight. You pay with a button. You open the jar, and the rumor inside is: "The mountain is grumpy." You already knew that. Then the boggart says it again, slower, looking sideways at the marsh road, and you realize it meant something else entirely.

choices.label: Take the jar to the dock folk and ask which road it meant

scene_three_rumours.narration: By sunset you have heard of three roads north. East, the queue at Stone Crossing is three days long, the trolls take a story instead of coins, and a river drake is charging double. Straight north, the old caravan road through the Plains is the shortest way, so everybody is on it, wheel to wheel. West, the frogfolk still pole travelers through the Whispering Marsh, if they like you, and the marsh has been noisy since the red night. "And mind the sky," adds the yeti. "The courier griffins are flying so overloaded with claim letters they can barely steer."

choices.label: Head back through the market, keeping one eye on the sky

scene_gutter_glint.narration: Right on cue, a courier griffin wobbles overhead with a mail sack bigger than it is. The sack splits, and letters flutter down over the market like pigeons. Something heavier lands in the gutter beside your boot with a little plink. It is a red stone the size of a plum, glittering, and warm, like toast just out of the fire. It is also, very faintly, humming.

choices.label: Pick it up and pocket it
Shout "Whose is this?"

scene_nobody_claims.narration: Eleven people say it is theirs. None of them can say what color it is. The griffin is already a dot over the sea, and the dot is not coming back. It seems the stone is yours, for now.

choices.label: Pocket it and find somewhere warm

scene_tavern.narration: The Empty Chair tavern is packed with prospectors. On a table in the middle, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows is waving her arms. "The gem-light fell upward! Only for a moment, but it did!" The whole room laughs, and two very polite stone trolls carry her out of the door, table and all. She keeps talking the whole way.

choices.label: Follow her outside
Tell her we saw it too!
Ask what it means. That is why we came, after all
Leave her be. There are gem-buyers to see

scene_scholar_believed.narration: The scholar stops wringing out her notes and stares at you. Then she hugs you, which is very wet, because she is a selkie and it is raining. "Professor Marrow Tidewell," she says, "and you are the first people who have believed me all week." She unpins the owl-feather clasp from her own coat and gives it to you, for clear thinking.

choices.label: Hear the whole theory

scene_scholar_theory.narration: Outside, Professor Tidewell draws on a napkin: a shape with eight sides, like a gem cut by somebody very careful. "The oldest stories tell of a seal, like a lid on a jar, with eight great facets. I think the mountain just threw seven of them across the realm, and everybody is selling them. The eighth is still in the mountain." Then she looks at your pocket, which is glowing slightly. "Oh," she says. "You've got one."

choices.label: Thank her, and think about it

choice_ember.narration: Gem-buyers line the whole quay. The biggest is Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk who gets about in a barrel on wheels, and she smells your warm red stone from ten stalls away. "Rush prices, darlings," she says, and names a number so big that a pigeon faints. Do we sell it, or keep it?

choices.label: Sell it to Madame Fenn
Haggle her up even higher, then sell
Keep it

choice_ember_sell_high.narration: You name a bigger number. Madame Fenn names a smaller one. You name a bigger one again, and a second pigeon faints. In the end she pays twice what she offered, laughs so hard her barrel rolls into a bollard, and throws in a brave whistle "for cheek, darlings." Then she writes your names in her little green book, twice.

choices.label: Take the clanking purse

scene_sold.narration: Madame Fenn pays with a purse so heavy it clanks, and throws in a hearthstone bead "for luck, darlings." Then she writes your names in a little green book. "I never forget a good seller," she says, and somehow you believe her. The stone goes into her barrel, still humming, and the humming goes with it.

choices.label: Go and spend some of it

scene_kept.narration: You close your hand around the stone. Still warm. Madame Fenn sighs a sigh so big her barrel rocks on its wheels. "Your loss, darlings. Or somebody's." The stone feels a little heavier now, the way a promise does.

choices.label: Go and get ready for the road

scene_market.narration: Every shop on the Outfitters' Steps is selling the same three things: boots, rope, and quickfoot laces. A faun cobbler called Tobble Reedpipe sings the price of each lace as he sells it, and every verse goes up a key. By the top of the steps he is squeaking.

choices.label: Haggle with Tobble
Buy the best laces outright. We're rich now!
Tell Tobble we're after a fresh start
Point out the fake laces on the next stall

scene_market_spot_fakes.narration: Your kitsune sniffs once and points. "Those are bootlaces painted yellow." The stall-keeper next door goes very red, packs up in about four seconds, and is never seen on the Outfitters' Steps again. Tobble is so grateful he presses real quickfoot laces on you and sings your names up the whole scale.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_fresh_start.narration: Tobble stops singing. "A fresh start," he says, and for once he just speaks. He has one too, he says. He used to make boots for a duke, and then he decided he liked laces better. He sells you the laces at last year's price and sings a small verse about beginnings that nearly rhymes.

choices.label: Lace up

scene_market_buy_outright.narration: You point at the best laces on the rack and pay without asking the price. Tobble is so startled he sings the price anyway, out of habit, a whole key too high. Three prospectors turn round to see who is rich. You try to look like you have always been rich.

choices.label: Lace up

check_haggle.prompt: Haggle with a cobbler who is singing the price

onSuccess.narration: You sing back, one key lower. Tobble is so delighted he sells you the laces at last week's price.

onFailure.narration: You haggle so hard that Tobble loses his place in the song and starts again from the top, twice. Somewhere in the muddle, money changes hands and something is wrapped in paper.

scene_laced.narration: The quickfoot laces go on, and right away your feet would like to be somewhere else, quickly. Tobble sings a little verse about you. It is very flattering and mostly does not rhyme.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

scene_lace_tangle.narration: You haggle so hard that Tobble gets muddled and sells you a honeycake instead of laces. You are not sure how that happened. Neither is Tobble. It is a very good honeycake, though.

choices.label: Find a bed for the night

rest_empty_chair.narration: You rent the last room in the Exchange, which is a cupboard under some stairs with a lovely view of the stairs. Somebody shares out supper. Through the wall, three people in three languages argue happily about the price of onions, and all three of them are right.

choices.label: Up at dawn for the caravan yard

scene_caravan_yard.narration: At dawn the caravan yard is a sea of wagons, all pointed north. The one with the most lanterns belongs to Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master whose sash is stitched all over with roads. She looks at the three of you the way she looks at weather. "Room for three," she says. "Why should it be you?"

choices.label: Tell her honestly why we're going
Lift the stuck wagon out of the mud
Offer to guard the lantern wagon
Bet we can load a wagon faster than anyone
Offer to carry the banner at the front

scene_caravan_yard_banner.narration: The banner is taller than any of you and heavier than it looks, and the wind off the harbor wants it very badly. You hold it up anyway. The whole yard turns to look at who is carrying the Longstride banner, and Hesper lets them look. "Front," she says. "Don't drop it."

choices.label: Take your place at the front

scene_caravan_yard_race.narration: A yeti crew bets you cannot load a wagon faster than they can. You load it in the time it takes them to argue about who goes first. Half of it is loaded upside down, but it is loaded. The yetis pay up in dried apples, and Hesper, very slightly, smiles.

choices.label: Collect your winnings

scene_caravan_yard_guard.narration: "The lantern wagon," says Hesper, "has been robbed twice this week and set on fire once." You say you will guard it anyway. She looks at you the way she looks at weather that has decided to be useful, and hands you a long pole with a hook on the end.

choices.label: Take up your post

scene_caravan_yard_lift_wagon.narration: You walk over to the wagon stuck in the mud, take hold of the back axle, and lift. The wagon comes up. So does the mud. So does a small faun who was sitting in the wagon eating breakfast, and who keeps eating it. Hesper watches the whole thing without a word, then nods once.

choices.label: Report for duty

check_signon.prompt: Tell a caravan master the truth and mean it

onSuccess.narration: Hesper listens to the whole answer, all the way to the end. Then she nods once, like a gate closing.

onFailure.narration: You get muddled halfway through and say "um" eleven times. Hesper is kind about it. Hesper is also busy.

scene_hired.narration: Hesper hands you each a lantern pole. "Crew," she says, which on a caravan means you eat first and sleep last. The wagons begin to roll, and the Exchange shrinks behind you into a bright muddle of roofs, with one lighthouse still pretending it saw nothing.

choices.label: Roll north

scene_turnip_wagon.narration: "Cargo, then," says Hesper, kindly. You ride north squashed into a wagon full of turnips, which is not glamorous, but it is north. One turnip rolls into your lap and stays there, like a cat.

choices.label: Roll north anyway

rest_northbound.narration: That night the caravan camps in the first of the Sunward Fields, where the grass smells of honey and everybody's boots still smell of the city. Far to the north the sky glows faintly red, like a coal somebody forgot to put out. Share out your things, patch each other up, and get some sleep. The road starts properly tomorrow.

llmHints.tone: gold-rush overture: bustling, funny, warm, a little mysterious about the red sky but never scary
forbidden: any one people owning or founding the Exchange
explaining what the gemstones really are

npcVoices.tidewell: Professor Marrow Tidewell, a selkie scholar with ink on both elbows; talks fast, draws on napkins, has been laughed out of better taverns and keeps going anyway
npcVoices.coralie_fenn: Madame Coralie Fenn, a merfolk gem-buyer in a barrel on wheels; calls everyone darlings, names enormous numbers cheerfully, never forgets a seller
npcVoices.tobble: Tobble Reedpipe, a faun cobbler who sings every price, going up a key each verse; delighted by anyone who sings back
npcVoices.hesper: Hesper Longstride, a centaur caravan master with a road-stitched sash; few words, listens to the whole answer, kind but busy
npcVoices.boggart: a rumor-selling boggart in a coat made of other coats; never says anything straight, always says it twice
npcVoices.lighthouse_keeper: a very old merfolk in a bathtub at the top of the lighthouse; firmly did not see anything
npcVoices.tour_guide: a centaur tour guide who loves the seventeen plaques and charges for every fact
npcVoices.mortar: Mortar, a stone troll noodle cook; stirs one full slow turn before answering anything, says very little, and means all of it
